tracks.name: AI Skills
tracks.blurb: Practical AI for people who run or work in a business: how the tools work, how to get real value from them, and how to automate safely.

courses.title: AI Foundations for Business Leaders
courses.desc: How large language models work, what they are good and bad at, what they cost, and how to pick the first problems worth solving.

courses.title: Working Smarter with AI Assistants
courses.desc: Prompt patterns, giving the model the right context, checking its output, and turning one-off chats into repeatable workflows.

courses.title: AI Agents & Automation
courses.desc: What AI agents are, how they use tools and connectors like MCP, and how to design automations that keep a human in the loop.

courses.title: Generative Coding in Practice
courses.desc: Use AI coding assistants to build and fix software faster, with the reviews and tests that keep the results trustworthy.

courses.title: Building with LLM APIs & RAG
courses.desc: Retrieval, embeddings, evaluation and cost control for teams building AI features into their own products.

courses.title: AI Governance & Responsible Use
courses.desc: Write an AI use policy people will follow, map it to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and handle data, vendors and disclosure.

tracks.name: Cryptography & PQC
tracks.blurb: How encryption actually protects your data, why quantum computers threaten it, and how to move to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) on a sensible timeline.

courses.title: Cryptography Essentials
courses.desc: Hashes, symmetric and public-key encryption, digital signatures and TLS, explained with everyday examples.

courses.title: The Quantum Threat to Encryption
courses.desc: What Shor's and Grover's algorithms would break, what "harvest now, decrypt later" means, and realistic timelines.

courses.title: Lattice-Based Cryptography Explained
courses.desc: The idea behind the new NIST post-quantum standards ML-KEM and ML-DSA, taught visually and without a math degree.

courses.title: Your Post-Quantum Migration Plan
courses.desc: Build a cryptography inventory, design for crypto-agility, test hybrid TLS, and ask vendors the right questions.

tracks.name: AI Security
tracks.blurb: The new risks that come with AI, from staff pasting data into chatbots to attackers hijacking AI agents, and the controls that work.

courses.title: Securing AI Use at Work
courses.desc: Shadow AI, data leaks, the account and retention settings that matter, and one page of AI rules your team will actually follow.

courses.title: Deepfakes & AI-Powered Phishing
courses.desc: Voice clones, fake video calls and AI-written lures, plus the verification habits that stop them.

courses.title: Prompt Injection & LLM Attacks
courses.desc: How attackers hijack AI apps with hidden instructions, mapped to the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025), and the defenses that hold up.

courses.title: The AI Supply Chain
courses.desc: Models, datasets, plugins and leaked API keys: where AI risk enters your business and how to control it.

courses.title: Securing AI Agents & MCP
courses.desc: Permissions, tool scoping, secrets and logging for AI agents that can take actions on your systems.

tracks.name: Cybersecurity Hot Topics
tracks.blurb: Deep dives into one specific corner of security at a time, often built around a real attack that made the news.

courses.title: Anatomy of a VPN Zero-Day
courses.desc: Why firewalls and VPN appliances are attackers' favorite door, traced step by step through recent real-world attack chains.

courses.title: Inside a $6 Billion Crypto Heist
courses.desc: How one engineer's compromised laptop led to the Binance theft, and what it teaches every business about privileged access.

courses.title: Passkeys & the End of Passwords

courses.title: Browser Extensions: the Overlooked Attack Surface
courses.desc: How harmless-looking add-ons hijack searches and data, and how to control them with browser policies.

courses.title: Ransomware Recovery: the First 72 Hours
courses.desc: Containment, backups, legal and insurance calls, communications, and the decision about whether to negotiate.

tracks.blurb: The science behind the technology everyone is talking about, explained clearly enough to share at dinner.

courses.title: The Science of the Fold: Inside the iPhone Duo
courses.desc: How a phone screen survives folding thousands of times: flexible OLED, ultra-thin cover layers, a hinge with more than 100 parts, and hiding the crease and the camera.

courses.title: Blockchain Beyond Bitcoin
courses.desc: How shared ledgers, consensus and smart contracts work, and where they are useful outside of cryptocurrency.

courses.title: 3D Printing: From Prototypes to Houses
courses.desc: Plastic, resin, metal and concrete printing, and how additive manufacturing is changing factories and construction.

courses.title: Quantum Computing for Non-Physicists
courses.desc: Qubits, superposition, entanglement and error correction, and what quantum computers can and cannot do yet.

courses.title: Sodium-Ion Batteries
courses.desc: Why batteries made from cheap, common materials like salt could reshape electric vehicles and grid storage.

courses.title: Inside a Hyperscale AI Data Center
courses.desc: The chips, networking, power and cooling behind the huge clusters that train and run AI models.

courses.title: Next-Gen Nuclear & Small Modular Reactors
courses.desc: New fuels, coolants and factory-built reactors, and why tech companies are signing up to buy their power.
